- If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction.
- If model shows rapid upward trend after a spike (e.g., 3+ consecutive days rising >0.5% per day), reduce forecast slope to avoid overshoot.
- When supply net is negative and bullish events dominate, model often underestimates upside; increase forecast baseline by 1–2% relative to recent mean.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.00) and model shows upward trend, flag as “sentiment mismatch” — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day.
- Mean reversion bias: if model forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 0.3–0.7% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >5% from model in first 5 days, adjust forecast to align with early sentiment peaks or troughs.
- When official events show high bearish sentiment (e.g., net bearish >30) and model is rising, apply “bearish drag” — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day for next 5 days.
